title: Avoiding 'Dead Air'
summary: We practised starting and ending conversations with people we don't know well, in formal and informal situations. We made correct questions for small talk and practised the stress and weak forms in them. We also learned phrases for giving suggestions and advice about our hometown.

grammar.title: Question word order
grammar.explain: In most questions, the auxiliary verb (do, does, are, is, have) comes before the subject. Question words like where, what and how come first. With 'have got', 'have' goes before the subject.
grammar.explain_ar: في معظم الأسئلة يأتي الفعل المساعد (do, does, are, is, have) قبل الفاعل. وأدوات الاستفهام مثل where وwhat وhow تأتي في بداية السؤال. ومع have got نضع have قبل الفاعل.
form: (Question word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb: Where do you come from?
(Question word) + be + subject: How was your flight? / Is this your first visit?
Have + subject + got + ...: Have you got any brothers or sisters?
Do + subject + have + ...: Do you have any hobbies?

examples.note: Informal question to someone you know.

examples.en: What do you do in your free time?
examples.note: First 'do' is the auxiliary, second 'do' is the main verb.
'Whereabouts' asks about the area, not the exact place.

examples.en: Is this your first visit to Singapore?
examples.note: With 'be', just put it before the subject.

examples.en: Do you like doing or watching sports?

mistakes.why: 'Have' goes before the subject with 'have got'.

mistakes.wrong: What you do in your free time?
mistakes.right: What do you do in your free time?
mistakes.why: You need the auxiliary 'do' after the question word.

quiz.q: Unscramble: come / where / you / do / from / ?

quiz.why: 'flight' is singular, past of be: was.

quiz.q: ___ you got any brothers or sisters?
quiz.why: With 'have got', the question starts with 'Have'.

quiz.q: What ___ you do in your free time?
___ do you work? (asking about the general area)
quiz.why: 'Whereabouts' asks where, in a less exact way.

grammar.title: Making suggestions and giving advice
grammar.explain: We use different phrases to suggest things to do. Be careful with the verb form after each phrase: some take the base verb and some take the -ing form.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم عبارات مختلفة لاقتراح أشياء للقيام بها. انتبه إلى شكل الفعل بعد كل عبارة: بعضها يأتي بعده الفعل المجرّد، وبعضها يأتي بعده الفعل بصيغة ing.
form: You should / You could / Why don't you + base verb: You should go to the zoo.
How about / Try / Have you tried + verb-ing: Try watching horse racing.
One thing I recommend is + noun / verb-ing
If I were you, I would / wouldn't + base verb

examples.en: You should definitely visit the old market.
Why don't you go to the zoo at the weekend?
How about going to the beach on Saturday?
Have you tried eating at the fish restaurant by the river?
If I were you, I wouldn't drive in the city centre.

mistakes.wrong: How about go to the zoo?
mistakes.right: How about going to the zoo?

mistakes.wrong: You should to visit the museum.
Why you don't try the market?
mistakes.right: Why don't you try the market?
mistakes.why: Word order: Why don't you + base verb.

mistakes.wrong: Have you tried to eat koshari? (meaning 'as an idea')

quiz.q: How about ___ horse racing on Sunday?
You ___ go to the zoo. It's great for families.
Try ___ the local food at the night market.
If I were you, I ___ take a taxi from the airport.
quiz.why: If I were you + would + base verb.
